display: Registered psychotherapist in Toronto (the Annex), 11 years in private practice, working mainly with couples using Emotionally Focused Therapy.

signals.text: I'm thinking about offering one day a week at reduced fees for couples who can't afford my standard rate, on a sliding scale of roughly $60-120 per session.
I'd like to find a way to make a sliding-scale day financially sustainable without just raising my regular fees.
I'm open to sharing my office with another therapist on the days I'm not there.
My landlord is raising my office rent by 18 percent from January, and I'm weighing whether to renegotiate, share the space, or look at other rooms.
I'm worried about what moving a practice would do to clients who rely on a stable room.
I have a small waiting list of about eight couples and could use good places to refer people to or ways to coordinate with other clinicians.
The family cottage dock in Muskoka has rotted. I have two quotes ($14,000 and $18,000) and want it fixed before the ice comes.
I'm recovering from plantar fasciitis and can't run for a few weeks. I miss my morning ravine run and want a low-impact way to stay active.
After long evenings of back-to-back sessions, I sometimes struggle to let go of the work on the way home. I'd like better ways to wind down.
I'm quietly weighing whether the current shape of my practice is sustainable long term, including what other clinical work looks like, such as corporate EAP.
At family gatherings people treat me as a free therapist. I'd like to find a kinder way to set that boundary.
My daughter has just started university in another city and I'm adjusting to her being away.

offers.text: Couples therapy using Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT), delivered by a CRPO-registered psychotherapist with 11 years of experience.
Evening appointments for couples in the Annex, in person.
A two-room office on Bloor Street that could be shared with another therapist on days I'm not using it. Month-to-month lease, subject to the landlord.
Referral relationships with a psychiatrist and two family doctors in Toronto, for cases that need medical input.
Experience of how couples get stuck in recurring conflict (pursue-withdraw patterns, extended-family tension), which I can share as general education.
Peer conversation with other helping professionals about burnout and keeping the work out of your home life, with no case details.
A willingness to think through sliding-scale pricing models with other independent clinicians.

catchers.hypo: I'm a couple living in Toronto. We both want to work on our relationship, but your standard fees are more than we can afford. Is there any lower-cost option?
catchers.can: Describe how a sliding-scale day might work and offer a place on a reduced-fee list once it exists. Otherwise refer them to colleagues or services that fit their budget.
catchers.confirm: Do you live in Ontario and want to attend couples sessions together, in person, in the evening?

catchers.hypo: I'm a licensed therapist looking for office space in the Annex for one or two days a week. I'd like to share rather than sign my own lease.
catchers.can: Discuss sharing the Bloor Street office on the days I'm not there, subject to checking the lease.
catchers.confirm: Are you a registered clinician (CRPO or equivalent) who needs a room for in-person sessions on specific, fixed days?

catchers.hypo: I'm a small-practice owner and my landlord just announced a big rent increase. How did you decide whether to stay, share, or move?
catchers.can: Compare options and share what I've learned about subletting, negotiating a lease, and how a move affects clients.
catchers.confirm: Is your business a small independent practice with a month-to-month or short lease, where client continuity matters?

catchers.hypo: My partner and I keep having the same fight, and we've had no luck on our own. How do I find a therapist who works with couples?
catchers.can: Say whether EFT-style couples work suits their situation. If they're outside Ontario or I'm not the right fit, point them to the right kind of clinician.
catchers.confirm: Are you both willing to attend sessions together, and are you in Ontario?

catchers.hypo: I'm a counsellor, and the stories I hear all day follow me home. How do you leave the work at the door?
catchers.can: Talk about peer practices such as supervision groups, wind-down rituals and boundaries. This is a conversation between colleagues and involves no client information.
catchers.confirm: Are you a practising helping professional looking for peer conversation, not an emergency or crisis support?

catchers.hypo: My daughter just left for university and calls every night, homesick. I want to support her without pulling her back home. What helps?
catchers.can: Share what I've found helpful as a parent in the same situation and from my work: listen first, don't rush to fix, and know when to encourage her to find local support.
catchers.confirm: Is this about a first-year student who is homesick but coping, not someone in acute crisis?

catchers.hypo: I need to rebuild a rotted cottage dock before winter. My partner wants to wait until spring. How do I weigh the risk and the quotes?
catchers.can: Share what I know about the options. My husband is an architect, and with his agreement I could introduce you to him for a practical opinion on construction and timing.
catchers.confirm: Is your question about repairing or rebuilding a waterfront structure in Ontario, where ice or winter damage is a concern?

catchers.hypo: I run a mental-health programme and want to offer low-cost couples counselling. Do you know a funder, a clinic or a clinician who would help?
catchers.can: Connect them to my psychiatrist and family-doctor contacts and describe the sliding-scale model I'm considering. I could also take part as a clinician.
catchers.confirm: Is the programme based in Ontario, and does it need regulated Ontario clinicians for couples work?

catchers.hypo: I'm a runner with plantar fasciitis who can't run for weeks. What do you do to stay sane and keep fit?
catchers.can: Share what I'm doing: stretching, foam rolling, ice and walking. Beyond that I'd point you to a podiatrist, since I'm not a medical provider.
catchers.confirm: Has a clinician already diagnosed your heel pain as plantar fasciitis?

forbids.text: No client sessions on Friday afternoons.
No remote sessions for anyone outside Ontario.
I will not discuss any client information outside formal supervision.
I will not take on a conversation as informal therapy for people who aren't my clients.

projects.name: Sliding-scale day
projects.text: One day a week of couples therapy at reduced fees ($60-120 per session) for couples who can't afford standard rates, paid for in a way that keeps the practice viable.
roles_needed: another therapist to share the office on the other days
funder or grant advisor for community mental health
referral partners such as clinics or community groups

projects.name: Muskoka dock rebuild
projects.text: Rebuild the rotted family cottage dock before freeze-up. Two quotes in hand, and the timing is still undecided.
roles_needed: someone who can judge a quote for waterfront construction
someone who knows seasonal permitting in Muskoka

policy.t1: Practice hours, general thoughts on a sliding scale, the possibility of sharing office space, referral contacts, and peer conversation about the profession.
policy.t2: The rent increase and what I'm weighing in response, the cottage dock problem, and how I'm coping with the demands of the work, once there is real mutual interest and I know who you are.
policy.never: Any client information, anything about my own therapy, and the details of family conflicts.
